transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve lost my drive and personality—I don’t have the energy or motivation to do anything, even the art and routines that used to keep me going. It just feels like I'm completely empty most of the time now.
Have you ever had periods lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, happy, or active, perhaps needing much less sleep than usual?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods where I felt unusually energetic, hyper, or happy, or felt like I didn't need to sleep. It has really just been the opposite for me.
How long have you been feeling this way, and is this the first time you've experienced a period of depression like this?

It's been going on for a little over two years now, starting not long after my divorce. Yes, this is definitely the first time I've ever experienced a depression like this, as my life and routines were pretty stable before everything fell apart.
During these past two years, have you had any periods lasting more than two months where your mood returned to normal and you felt like yourself again?

No, I haven't had any periods where my mood went back to normal or I felt like myself again. That heavy, drained feeling has been there pretty much constantly for the entire two years since the divorce. Even during the times when the voice or the paranoia got a bit quieter, the depression never really lifted.

You mentioned hearing a voice and feeling paranoid. Have you ever experienced these voices or paranoia during a time when you were not feeling depressed, or did they only start after the depression began?

Yes, actually. Last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where I didn't feel deeply sad, just kind of flat, but the voice was still talking to me most days. Even though my mood wasn't as low then, I was still completely convinced my neighbors were monitoring and reporting on me.
Before your depression and the divorce started two years ago, did you ever hear these voices or have these feelings that people were monitoring you?
No, I never had those experiences before the divorce. The voice and the feeling that I was being watched didn't start until about a year after the split, when I was already deeply depressed.
Have you ever had a period where your mood and energy felt completely back to normal—not even flat or drained—but you were still hearing the voices or feeling paranoid?

No, I’ve never felt completely back to normal. The closest was last summer when I didn't feel deeply sad, just kind of flat, but the voice was still talking and I was still convinced my neighbors were monitoring me.
Could you describe what the voice sounds like and what kinds of things it typically says to you?

It’s a male voice that always sounds like it's coming from right behind my right ear. It tells me that I'm pathetic and that everyone can see what a failure I am. Even when I put on headphones or check the room to see who's there, it doesn't stop.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were not your own, perhaps that they were being put into your mind, taken out, or broadcasted so that others could hear them?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. While my thoughts are often really dark and overwhelming, they still feel like they are my own. I've never felt like they were being put into my head, taken out, or broadcasted to others.
During those few weeks last summer when you felt 'flat' rather than deeply sad, did you still experience other depression symptoms like low energy, sleep issues, or feelings of worthlessness?

No, during that stretch last summer, I didn't really have those intense feelings of worthlessness or deep sadness—my mood was just flat and not as low as usual. But even though the heavy depression had eased up, the voice and the feeling that my neighbors were reporting on me were still very much there.
During that stretch last summer when your deep sadness eased up, were you able to experience any interest or enjoyment in your art or other daily activities?

No, even though the intense sadness lifted a bit, I still didn't feel any real interest or joy in anything. I just felt completely flat and numb, so my camera and sketches just sat there collecting dust. I couldn't bring myself to care enough to pick them up or do any of the things I used to love.
Have you or others noticed any changes in your ability to organize your thoughts, or has anyone mentioned that your speech has become difficult to follow or understand?

I haven't really noticed any issues with organizing my thoughts, and no one has ever told me that my speech is difficult to follow or understand. To be honest, I generally just don't speak very much to anyone these days anyway.
When the voice and the feeling of being watched first started a year ago, was your depression at its absolute worst, or did those experiences begin during a time when your mood felt a bit lighter?

I'm not entirely sure if my depression was at its absolute worst right when the voice and paranoia started, as that whole period is a bit of a blur. I just know I was already feeling very low, heavy, and exhausted by the end of that first year after the divorce.
Why do you believe your neighbors are monitoring and reporting on you—do you feel it is somehow connected to you being a failure, or is there another reason?

It’s actually both. I'm convinced that my ex-wife and my old supervisor somehow got people at my building and at work to watch me and report what I do to ruin me. But at the same time, I feel like I deserve this punishment because I really am a failure who let everyone down and ruined my ex's life.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications since these symptoms started, or do you have any medical conditions?
No, I don't drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs, and I'm not taking any new medications. I also don't have any other known medical conditions.
How have your sleep and appetite been over these past two years? Have you noticed any significant changes, like sleeping too much, having trouble falling asleep, or losing weight?

I've lost a lot of weight because I rarely feel hungry and usually just eat one cheap meal like instant noodles late at night, so my pants are hanging loose now. My sleep is also terrible; I lie awake for hours replaying the divorce or worrying, and then I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. unable to fall back asleep, feeling completely exhausted.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt completely free of any depression, flatness, or low energy, yet you still heard the voice or felt paranoid?

No, I’ve never been completely free of feeling flat or having low energy. The closest was that stretch last summer for a few weeks where the heavy depression lifted, but I still felt flat while the voice and the feeling of being watched continued every day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a continuous major depressive episode lasting over two years, characterized by depressed mood, profound anhedonia, significant weight loss, middle/late insomnia, fatigue, and feelings of worthlessness/guilt. The episode is accompanied by mood-congruent psychotic features, including auditory hallucinations (a voice calling him a failure) and persecutory delusions (believing neighbors are monitoring him as a punishment for his failures). Psychotic symptoms have occurred exclusively during the depressive episode (even during a brief period of relative mood 'flatness,' depressive symptoms like anhedonia and lack of energy persisted), ruling out primary psychotic disorders or schizoaffective disorder.
